主要内容: Arch Coal Inc., the second-largest coal reserve holder in the U.S., filed for bankruptcy on January 11, 2016, as the country continues to shift toward cheaper, cleaner-burning natural gas. This move marks another blow to U.S. coal miners, who have been struggling with the decline in demand due to the rise of natural gas and stricter pollution regulations. The company has been losing money since 2012 and has reached an agreement with a majority of its senior lenders to erase $4.5 billion in debt from its balance sheet, allowing it to continue operations without interruption. The bankruptcy filing highlights the ongoing challenges faced by the coal industry in the U.S., as it competes with cleaner energy sources.
